prompt: A contributor proposes that `beacon build` also pick up guardrails and commands from `CLAUDE.md` and `.cursor/rules`, and that `beacon init` copy the values it discovers (license, CI test command, README description) straight into the generated beacon.yaml. What settled decision currently governs which project files Beacon reads and what `beacon init` writes, what does it rule out, and which docs, source files and tests state or enforce it?

points: init writes only fields maintainer must answer
discovered values read at build time

gold_citations.quote: **Declared sources (2026-09-23).** A beacon reads `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `SECURITY.md` as `declared` sources
reads them on every run instead of copying them into ``beacon.yaml``, so they cannot go stale there.
`src/beacon/core/scaffold.py`: `beacon init` writes only the judgment fields, empty; discovered values stay in the init report and are never frozen into `beacon.yaml`.
# Agent-vendor files such as CLAUDE.md are never read.
It never reads agent-vendor files (`CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules` and similar); those should only point to `AGENTS.md`.
Discovered facts are reported, never frozen into beacon.yaml as intent.
A beacon reads `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `SECURITY.md` as `declared` sources
`beacon init` writes only the fields a maintainer must answer

gold_citations.item: discovered values read at build time
gold_citations.quote: everything a project's files state is read at build time, never copied into `beacon.yaml`

notes: The decision is recorded in docs/beacon-open-standard.md section 10 'Settled decisions' and implemented in the 2026-09-23 near-zero authoring P0 change (.agent/CHANGELOG.md). What it ruled out: reading agent-vendor files and freezing discovered values into beacon.yaml (previously init rendered discovered values into the starter manifest; the scaffold.py module docstring still describes rendering a DiscoveryResult into beacon.yaml, so the CHANGELOG is the clearer statement for scaffold.py). The 'declared sources' point is loose on purpose; reviewers may want to tighten it.
